discovery: Giant tunnel magnetoresistance in crystalline MgO magnetic tunnel junctions

nominees.name: Stuart S. P. Parkin
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Microstructure Physics, Halle, Germany

nominees.name: Shinji Yuasa
nominees.affiliation: National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST), Tsukuba, Japan

motivation: Butler predicted that symmetry filtering of Bloch states in epitaxial Fe/MgO/Fe junctions would give tunnel magnetoresistance of thousands of percent. In 2004 Parkin and Yuasa independently showed room-temperature TMR near 200% in MgO-barrier junctions, far beyond what amorphous alumina barriers could deliver. This showed that coherent spin-dependent tunnelling, not just interface spin polarization, controls the effect, and it opened a new field of spin-filtering physics. The impact on technology was immediate and very large. MgO junctions became the read sensor in essentially every hard-disk drive. They are the storage element of spin-transfer-torque MRAM, now made in leading foundries, and the basis of spin-torque oscillators and emerging neuromorphic devices. Having helped bring the first commercial MRAM to market, I can attest that this discovery turned spintronics from a laboratory curiosity into a manufacturable, scalable information technology. It combines deep physics with world-changing applications.
